Attaching our insurer contact details and the current COI template for reference. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks Hannah — drafting proposed limited redline and a short certificate acceptance checklist. Quick notes for the thread: 

- Subcontractor COI: we can accept COIs issued in the subcontractor's name so long as (a) Orchid Cloud is listed as an Additional Insured on the policy or via endorsement; (b) the policy provides primary and non-contributory coverage as to Orchid; and (c) coverage limits meet or exceed the Order Form minimums. Suggested clause to add to the Order Form: 

  "For clarity, Customer may satisfy insurance obligations by providing Evidence of Insurance issued in the name of a designated subcontractor provided such evidence names the Customer as an Additional Insured and the subcontractor's policy meets all coverage types and limits required in the Order Form."

- Retroactive / prior acts: If Orchid requires retroactive coverage or prior acts coverage for a subcontractor, require explicit insurer attestation in the COI/endorsement.

- SLA carve-out language (short): 

  "Planned Maintenance Exclusion: Scheduled maintenance windows exceeding six (6) consecutive hours will be excluded from calculation of service credits provided Customer receives at least forty-eight (48) hours advance notice. Such exclusions shall not exceed two (2) events per calendar quarter without mutual written consent."

- Operational step: we need broker contact and a scanned COI/endorsement. We'll also perform a quick limit check and confirm acceptance within 2 business days of receipt.

Attached is a suggested redline (docx) with inline edits for your counsel. If Orchid legal wants changes, please send their redline back — we aim to keep the change narrow and Order Form-scoped.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Compliance & Contracts — Redwood Inference
